decisions.reason: The pinned graph.py defines create_deep_agent as a Python agent factory function; source declaration does not imply a deployed instance.
The factory body returns an LlmAgent expression on invocation; this establishes a source constructor site, not a startup or deployed instance count.
Within the static subagent builder loop, each processed spec reaches an LlmAgent constructor; actual execution and spec count are unobserved.
The dynamic-spec builder returns an LlmAgent when executed on the relevant runtime path; the source is a factory, not evidence tasks ran.
The def statement merely declares create_deep_agent; it does not construct or deploy an agent at module import time.
AgentTool(agent=agent) wraps an existing passed LlmAgent object without calling a second LlmAgent constructor.
A SubAgentSpec definition is configuration data, not proof that an LlmAgent instance was created in the deployed configuration.
DeepAgentConfig declares delegation_mode static by default; callers may override the configuration, so this is a default only.
The explicit predicate limits the static subagent builder branch to delegation_mode static or both.
The static builder call sets include_general_purpose=True; the separate name-deduplication condition still applies.
The builder checks whether general_purpose is already in the sanitized name set before appending the default spec.
After creating a sub_agent from its spec, the static builder appends AgentTool(agent=sub_agent); this is a declared wrapper relation.
The predicate gates addition of register-subagent and dynamic-task tool factories to dynamic or both modes.
Inside the dynamic-enabled branch, source calls create_register_subagent_tool to build a tool; no actual agent registration is shown.
Inside the dynamic-enabled branch, source calls create_dynamic_task_tool; this registers a task mechanism, not an enumerated runtime subagent.
The parent constructor receives a list assembled from core_tools plus subagent_tools; membership depends on earlier branches.
The static builder is guarded by static or both, so the displayed dynamic-only source branch does not build static AgentTool wrappers.
The register-subagent and dynamic-task source branch requires dynamic or both and is not traversed for static-only mode.
The general_purpose prompt description is added for every valid delegation mode, including dynamic-only where static tool construction is skipped.
The wrapper is an AgentTool around a prebuilt object; this edge is not evidence of a second LlmAgent constructor.
The source passes cfg.delegation_mode through the factory, but the deployed caller configuration and execution context were not observed.
Defining a registration tool factory is not evidence which dynamic subagents were registered in a live session.
The callback is constructed from interrupt_on, but installed SDK behavior, configured approvals and effect on runtime invocations are unverified.
The constructed tool list is not proof all functions are reachable or approved in an installed deployed runtime with concrete identities and controls.
